newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Volumes dry up, premiums hold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Volumes dry up, premiums hold.

text.p: Turnover in major U.S. index options dried up Friday ahead of the weekend and a raft of economic reports scheduled for next week, but volatilities remained firm, with only slight erosion in premiums, traders said.
"It's very, very slow," said one index options trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange. "Volatility has creeped up today. Usually volatility dips ahead of the weekend."
He said market uncertainty ahead of next week's economic reports, which will be highlighted by Friday's jobs report for April, was keeping volatilities firm.
"There may be a little bit of time decay, but premiums are holding up pretty well," the trader said.
At around 1355 CDT/1855 GMT, the Dow industrial average was down 30 points at about 6,763 after hitting a session low of 6,729.
Among broader indices, the S&P 100 fell 2.34 to 751.90 and the S&P 500 lost 2.70 to 768.48.
June S&P 500 futures were down 3.85 at 772.50 after falling to a session low of 769.25. Traders pegged the next major support level at 766.
One firm pegged fair value for June S&Ps at 4.20 points over cash, with buy programs at 5.80 points over and sell programs at 3.40 points over.
The most active OEX option was the May 750 put, which traded about 4,000 contracts. The May 750 call traded roughly 3,330 and the May 740 put traded 3,265, rounding out the most actives.
Overall, put volume at 1330 CDT/1830 GMT was 30,959 contracts, compared with call volume of 23,411.
Among SPX options, put volume was 29,938 against call volume of 9,603.
Trading in SPX options was led by the May 700 put, where more than 4,300 contracts changed hands.

Among the economic reports scheduled to be released next week are the first quarter employment cost index, March durable goods orders, April consumer confidence, April purchasing managers data and the April unemployment report.
